$comment: DREDGE cross-repo dependency synchronization configuration anchored to ISS orbital telemetry
name: DEPENDADREDGEABOT Sync Network
description: Cross-repository dependency synchronization configuration for the DREDGE ecosystem, anchored to ISS orbital telemetry for deterministic, globally-coherent update scheduling.

sync_strategy.name: Orbital Coherence
sync_strategy.description: All repositories in the sync network update their dependencies on the same schedule, anchored to the ISS orbital clock at 03:10 UTC. This ensures consistent dependency versions propagate across the ecosystem in a single daily pass, preventing version drift between sibling projects.

grouping.rationale: Grouping reduces PR noise by batching related dependency bumps into single PRs per ecosystem group, keeping the review queue manageable while still surfacing security patches promptly.

sync_network.description: Repositories participating in the synchronized update schedule. All members share the same Dependabot schedule and ISS telemetry anchor.

iss_telemetry_integration.description: ISS orbital telemetry is fetched daily at 03:10 UTC and logged alongside each dependency sync run. The telemetry provides a deterministic, real-world timestamp anchor that is independent of any single cloud provider's clock, making sync events globally verifiable.

outputs.latitude: ISS latitude at time of sync trigger (degrees)
outputs.longitude: ISS longitude at time of sync trigger (degrees)
outputs.velocity_kms: ISS orbital velocity in km/s (~7.66 km/s nominal)
outputs.timestamp: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of telemetry reading

orbital_coherence_philosophy.manifesto: The International Space Station completes one orbit of Earth every ~90 minutes at an altitude of ~408 km and a velocity of ~7.66 km/s. It does not ask whether its dependencies are up to date. It simply orbits — reliably, predictably, perpetually. DEPENDADREDGEABOT aspires to the same orbital discipline: updates arrive on schedule, in coherent formation, leaving no repository behind in the gravity well of stale semver.
principles: Synchronised schedules eliminate version drift between sibling repositories.
Grouping reduces PR entropy — fewer PRs, more signal, less noise.
A 03:10 UTC trigger precedes most CI peak hours, minimising merge conflicts.
Docker updates are weekly because container base images are heavier cargo and deserve deliberate review.
ISS telemetry is the universal timestamp — it belongs to no cloud, no region, no vendor.
Orbital coherence is not a metaphor. It is an engineering discipline.
